Intelligence · factors that work now

Agents that pick the factors that work now.

factor.timing ranks a 79-factor zoo — price, volume, fundamental, and FRED macro families — by rolling Rank IC, and surfaces the signals working right now. Every factor is formalized, IC-tested, multiple-testing-checked, de-correlated, and logged with author, timestamp, and the economic-story gate decision.

Research is a debate, not a single voice.

A deep dive convenes technical, fundamental, sentiment, and valuation analysts — and, when you ask, a panel of investing legends. They argue opposing cases, then Inalpha synthesizes the disagreement into one decision on record.

Optional · a panel of investing legends

Pluggable methods · agent skills

Beyond the panel, agents load research playbooks as skills — a supply-chain lens, a methodology you bring in — read only when a case calls for it. Knowledge plugs in; tokens aren't spent on what isn't in play.

04
Evolution · written, sandboxed, mutated

Agents write the strategy — then rewrite it to beat itself.

An agent writes a full strategy in Python. Three sandbox gates clear it before a single backtest runs. Then it mutates under a multi-objective fitness, so no one metric can be gamed — only strategies that beat the baseline survive.

Three sandbox gates
1AST audit

no os / eval / jailbreak imports

2Isolated subprocess

runs walled off from the kernel

3Strategy contract

must subclass + implement on_bar

Multi-objective fitness
sharpe + 0.3·calmar − 0.1·turnover − 1.0·(maxDD > 30%)
mutate · evaluate · keep what beats the baseline
Quality gate

Before promotion a gate scores the candidate against the baseline; below bar, the agent auto-pivots and rewrites once — only what clears ships. Survivors can be cross-validated — WalkForward / Purged / Combinatorial CV with a Deflated Sharpe — so an edge has to hold across many out-of-sample paths, not one lucky window.

05
Robustness · the overfitting gauntlet

Survive the gauntlet,
or it isn't an edge.

Picking the best of many trials is itself how you overfit. So every stage — factor selection, strategy selection, parameters, out-of-sample — carries its own statistical correction, not a single backtest you fell in love with.

core enemy·multiple-testing bias
01 / Backtest
  • CPCV · purge + embargo
  • Deflated Sharpe · N-trial corrected
  • Bootstrap Sharpe 95% CI
  • parameter-neighborhood sensitivity

kills a lucky window can't pose as an edge

02 / Factors
  • null-IC selection benchmark
  • Benjamini–Hochberg FDR
  • economic-story gate
  • ρ < 0.85 de-correlation

kills a data-mined ghost can't reach the library

03 / Evolution
  • multi-objective fitness
  • drawdown veto
  • turnover penalty
  • buy-and-hold baseline race

kills no single metric can be gamed

04 / Look-ahead
  • point-in-time fundamentals
  • FRED release-lag table
  • bars truncated to as_of
  • test fold ends on the latest bar

kills a backtest never sees tomorrow

06
Unified kernel · same code, three modes

One codebase.
Three modes.

Strategy code is written once. Backtest, paper, and the live runner all share it — swap only the Clock and the Gateway. Business logic never changes; divergence can only come from physical reality — slippage, latency, data precision.

strategy = MomentumStrategy(params)
clock =SimClock(bars_2024)
gateway =SimGateway()
engine.run(strategy, clock, gateway)
only clock + gateway change · your strategy never does

07
Trust boundary · the moat

The AI proposes.
It never places the order.

Every order intent walks a one-way path: the agent drafts a plan, a rule you set (or you) approves it, and only then does a single-use, expiring token unlock execution. The model has no tool that reaches the order book directly — not after a jailbreak, not after a hallucination.

Order book
guard-stop · Framework backstop

Independent of strategy logic, the framework caps every position at a −20% hard stop — applied in backtest too, so the drawdown you see is the drawdown you'd live. Its liquidations clear the risk gate only when triple-signed (SELL · guard tag · guard- order prefix), so nothing can spoof its way past the boundary.

── Where we are honest with you

  • 01Autonomous paper runner + cross-currency cash: promoted strategies trade a simulated multi-currency account on live bars, machine-approved through plan/exec, with full decision replay
  • 02A 79-factor library with lineage tracking and decay alerts — factors are IC-monitored and de-correlated; alerts only warn, they never move your book
  • 03Framework position guard: a −20% hard stop applied in backtest and paper alike, independent of strategy logic
  • 04RiskEngine enforced at the paper HTTP boundary: notional cap / price deviation / drawdown veto / real exchange calendars across every market
  • 05Point-in-time fundamentals: financials filtered by report period + release lag, so a backtest never sees a number before it was public (akshare live; yfinance v1 not yet PIT, flagged in place)
  • 06No real-capital deployment — the runner trades a paper account, orders matched locally; every step passes plan/exec approval and lands on disk
